Benchmark: M-series laptop and desktop, 2B/4B/9B, prefill and decode, sustained tokens/s, memory bandwidth, joules/token

results.title: Strix Halo: native RDNA3.5 low-bit inference (HIP vs Vulkan)
results.author: zeekay
results.body_snippet: gfx1151 (Ryzen AI Max) is an experimental target in the datacenter-oriented ROCm kernel libraries; specialise rather than port CDNA kernels. Native packed-ternary HIP kernels, attention tuned for RDNA wavefronts, fused GDN ops, GPU residency and unified-memory behaviour; compare against Vulkan and llama.cpp on the same machine instead of assuming ROCm wins. References: AMD AITER, ROCm architecture specs, TileLang HIP backend. Benchmark: Ryzen AI Max+ 395, 4B/9B/27B, M=1/8/64/256, 5K/30K contexts

results.title: Table-lookup ternary inference on ARM and x86 CPUs (T-MAC style)
results.author: zeekay
results.body_snippet: Compute low-bit products with lookup tables and bit operations instead of expanding weights: a native ternary LUT operator for ARM NEON, ARM dot-product instructions, AVX2 and AVX-512 with hardware-specific register tiling. References: T-MAC (arXiv 2407.00088), BitNet runtime. The paper's gains are workload-specific. Benchmark: CPU-only on a phone-class ARM SoC, Raspberry Pi 5, a laptop and a Ryzen AI laptop; the complete network, not just low-bit GEMM. Proof: better sustained tokens/s and joule

results.title: NPU-native low-bit inference for phones and AI PCs
results.author: zeekay
results.body_snippet: NPUs lose their advantage on unsupported operators, format conversion and synchronisation. Build an export path from our supported operators to Core ML and Qualcomm QNN (ExecuTorch delegates) and partition the graph only when the avoided compute exceeds the transfer and sync overhead. Test whether a delegate runs compressed ternary arithmetic or silently dequantises to a larger representation. References: T-MAN (arXiv 2511.11248), ExecuTorch. Benchmark: iPhone and Snapdragon devices, cold load,

results.title: Kernel laboratory: automatic shape-specialised tuning for CUDA, HIP and Metal
results.author: zeekay
results.body_snippet: Search tile sizes, warp/wave layouts, group sizes, fusion choices and dispatch thresholds per model shape and hardware target, and export winners as versioned reproducible backend implementations. Candidate tools: TileLang (CUDA, HIP, Metal), CUTLASS/CuTe, AITER; a research tool, not a wholesale production dependency. Proof: tuned kernels beat the existing baselines end-to-end; configurations that only win microbenchmarks are rejected. Scorecard for every run: cold and warm TTFT, p50/p95 inter-t

results.title: Fused Gated DeltaNet and recurrent-state kernels
results.author: zeekay
results.body_snippet: The hybrid attention/GDN architecture makes this central: fuse GDN gating, causal convolution, recurrent-state read/update and selected projections; specialise single-token decode, prefill and multi-token verification separately; study compact recurrent-state representations only where accuracy survives testing. References: Flash Linear Attention (Gated DeltaNet, FlashQLA, GDN variants). Benchmark: kernel launch count, recurrent-state bandwidth, M=1/8/16, numerical parity, speculative rollback c

results.title: Mixed-precision and activation-aware quantization per layer
results.author: zeekay
results.body_snippet: Minimum bits everywhere is not always best quality-per-byte or fastest. Choose per layer between ternary, INT4, INT8 and BF16; test higher precision for embeddings, output heads, gates and selected projections. References: SpinQuant (learned rotations), AWQ (activation-aware), LLM Compressor (mixed precision, pruning, quantization-aware distillation). Benchmark: quality at equal memory, actual model size, cold TTFT, warm throughput, energy; instruction following, code-edit accuracy, multilingual

results.title: 2-bit and 4-bit KV cache compression
results.author: zeekay
results.body_snippet: Optional quantized KV format in the existing paged cache: 8-bit and 4-bit first, then 2-bit with a higher-precision recent-token window; keys and values quantised differently (KIVI, arXiv 2402.02750). Recurrent GDN state compression is a separate numerical research problem: a KV recipe does not establish it is safe. Benchmark: 5K/30K/128K context, peak resident memory, decode bandwidth, code-generation correctness, retrieval fidelity. Scorecard for every run: cold and warm TTFT, p50/p95 inter-to

results.title: Persistent, shareable prefix caches for multi-turn agents
results.author: zeekay
results.body_snippet: Reuse across requests, sessions and compatible workers: prefix-aware scheduling, versioned KV and GDN-state snapshots, tiered storage (RadixAttention, arXiv 2312.07104; tiered KV persistence). Cache keys include model/checkpoint identity, tokenizer, quantization, position encoding, runtime configuration and tenant authorisation; cross-tenant reuse must never expose private state. Benchmark: the 20-turn developer-agent workload, repeated repository reads, common system prompts, tool-result change

results.title: Long-context cache selection: retrieval heads vs streaming heads
results.author: zeekay
results.body_snippet: Classify retrieval heads (need full context) and streaming heads (short history) and compare with the current LSA implementation (DuoAttention, arXiv 2410.10819). Needs offline calibration per model; not a safe universal transformation. Benchmark: repository-level QA, distant-reference retrieval, needle-in-a-haystack, code edits needing old context, long-context prefill cost. Scorecard for every run: cold and warm TTFT, p50/p95 inter-token latency, full agent-loop wall time, peak memory, energy

results.title: Hardware-specialised attention: FlashAttention-4, FlashInfer, cascade attention
results.author: zeekay
results.body_snippet: Benchmark paged attention, LSA and the dense components of hybrid models against FlashInfer (paged, ragged, cascade, prefill/decode) and FlashAttention-4 (Blackwell pipelining, MLSys 2026); explore shared-prefix cascade attention and fused prefill/decode for batch serving. Results are per architecture: Hopper, Blackwell, GB10 and consumer RTX separately; B200 numbers are not GB10 assumptions. Proof: measurable end-to-end serving speedup, not kernel TFLOPS. Scorecard for every run: cold and warm

results.title: CUDA graphs for the linear-attention decode path, verification and variable shapes
results.author: zeekay
results.body_snippet: Make the LSA decode path graph-capturable where state and shapes permit, then graph-compatible speculative verification with bounded shape buckets and persistent input/output buffers. Graph memory-lifetime fixes are hard requirements. References: breakable CUDA graphs and linear-attention execution in current serving engines. Benchmark: LSA with/without graphs at 8K/16K/30K/64K, capture overhead, memory, p95 latency, sanitizer validation. Proof: lower 30K-context decode latency with no graph-lif

results.title: Next-generation speculative decoding: feature-level drafts (EAGLE-3) and workload-aware draft selection
results.author: zeekay
results.body_snippet: We already have adaptive block drafting, MTP, suffix/prompt lookup and stand-down. The gap is choosing the draft source and verification shape: evaluate trained feature-level drafts (EAGLE-3, arXiv 2503.01840) for larger variants and select between prompt lookup, neural drafts and plain decoding by expected useful tokens per millisecond. Published speedups are model- and GPU-specific. Benchmark: mixed prose/code, 4B/9B/27B, acceptance, verification overhead, output correctness, full agent-loop t

results.title: Continuous batching, chunked prefill and latency-aware scheduling
results.author: zeekay
results.body_snippet: A fast single-user runtime can waste most GPU capacity under simultaneous requests. Token-budget scheduling with chunked prefill, decode prioritisation, admission control and KV-aware batching; prefill is compute-heavy and decode bandwidth-heavy, so the scheduler accounts for both. Keep single-user latency targets separate from datacenter throughput settings. Benchmark: 1/4/16/64/256 simultaneous requests, long/short mixes, p95 TTFT, inter-token latency, throughput per GPU, SLO completion rate.

results.title: Heterogeneous memory, CPU/GPU offload and cold-start minimisation
results.author: zeekay
results.body_snippet: Compressed-weight residency, memory mapping, asynchronous layer/expert prefetch, CPU/GPU execution partitioning; on unified-memory systems avoid copies between views of the same memory (PowerInfer, SOSP 2024; hybrid CPU/GPU inference paths). The best partitioning differs between discrete GPUs and unified-memory laptops. Benchmark: models that barely fit, fully fit and exceed GPU memory; cold start, page faults, sustained decode, energy. Scorecard for every run: cold and warm TTFT, p50/p95 inter-

results.title: Fused MoE execution, expert paging and expert-parallel communication
results.author: zeekay
results.body_snippet: Grouped expert GEMM, fused router/top-K dispatch, expert prefetch, hotness caching, distributed expert routing, low-bit experts without repeated expansion (DeepGEMM, DeepEP, ROCm MoE kernels). Applies to MoE architectures only. Benchmark: active experts per token, routing overhead, cache hit rate, grouped GEMM throughput, load imbalance, per-GPU throughput by concurrency. Scorecard for every run: cold and warm TTFT, p50/p95 inter-token latency, full agent-loop wall time, peak memory, energy per

results.title: Native sparse attention and multi-head latent attention
results.author: zeekay
results.body_snippet: Compare token-sparse, block-sparse and latent-attention kernels (FlashMLA, FlashInfer sparse/MLA) with LSA for models that use compatible attention representations; the latest kernels have changed architecture and KV-format requirements, so compatibility is explicit. For future model designs, decide whether latent KV or learned sparse attention is worth training for. Benchmark: 32K-256K context, prefill complexity, decode bandwidth, indexing overhead, long-context reasoning quality. Scorecard fo

results.title: Disaggregated prefill/decode and KV transport
results.author: zeekay
results.body_snippet: Keep the existing engine and control plane; add transfer-capable KV blocks, placement-aware routing and separately scalable prefill and decode pools (shared-KV serving architectures). Before moving a request compare saved compute against transfer time, network overhead and destination cache capacity. Benchmark: 2-8 GPU nodes, transfer bandwidth, prefill/decode interference, throughput per dollar, p95 TTFT. A cloud-scale item, not a laptop priority. Scorecard for every run: cold and warm TTFT, p5

results.title: Power-aware inference: DVFS and thermal stability policy
results.author: zeekay
results.body_snippet: On phones and thin laptops peak performance collapses under sustained load. A device policy choosing backend, model size, thread count, speculative mode and supported power controls from current thermal conditions (EnerInfer 2026; PELM, SenSys 2026: frequency scaling with speculative verification depth). Controls differ by OS, driver and permissions. Benchmark: first-token latency, sustained tokens/s at 1/5/15 minutes, energy per committed token, post-throttle performance. Scorecard for every ru

results.title: Model co-design for the edge: early exits, structured sparsity, quantization-aware distillation
results.author: zeekay
results.body_snippet: Research separate edge-focused model variants with early-exit supervision (LayerSkip, ACL 2024), structured sparsity where hardware accelerates it, and quantization-aware training/distillation (model-optimizer toolchains). LICENSING: the released LayerSkip research code is CC BY-NC and must not be copied into our commercial Apache-2.0 stack; use the paper to guide an independent implementation or obtain rights first. Benchmark: quality at fixed model size, fixed memory bandwidth and fixed energy

results.title: Incremental entity-relationship indexing (LightRAG)
results.author: zeekay
results.body_snippet: Extract typed entities and relationships from documents, Git commits, agent outputs and operational events, and update only the affected subgraph when a document or file changes. References: LightRAG (EMNLP 2025, arXiv 2410.05779; MIT). Benchmark: incremental ingest latency, relationships extracted per dollar, duplicate entity rate, answer accuracy and retrieval latency vs ordinary hybrid search. Shared rules for the retrieval and memory program: a source document, repository blob, Git commit, a

results.title: Associative memory by bounded Personalized PageRank (HippoRAG 2)
results.author: zeekay
results.body_snippet: Seed graph traversal from entities found in the query and retrieve related facts, files, events and evidence with bounded Personalized PageRank, weighting relationships by relevance and reliability. Example: 'Which change caused the CUDA graph memory alias?' joins the failure, kernel behaviour, allocator assumptions, a PR and the regression test. References: HippoRAG (arXiv 2405.14831), HippoRAG 2 (arXiv 2502.14802; MIT). Benchmark: HotpotQA, MuSiQue, custom cross-repository incident questions;

results.title: Community detection and hierarchical summaries for global questions (GraphRAG)
results.author: zeekay
results.body_snippet: Offline community detection, hierarchical summarisation and incremental summary invalidation for corpus-wide questions ('what are the largest sources of engineering regressions across our repositories?'); not the default path for exact lookups. Caution: the reference implementation (MIT) describes itself as research software in maintenance mode and indexing can be expensive. Reference: From Local to Global: Graph RAG (arXiv 2404.16130). Benchmark: cross-document synthesis accuracy, coverage, tok

results.title: Temporal and bitemporal knowledge graph with provenance (Graphiti)
results.author: zeekay
results.body_snippet: Store every edge with valid time (when the fact was true), transaction time (when we learned it) and evidence pointers, so 'PR #47 was open at 10 AM' and 'PR #47 is merged now' coexist and nothing is deleted. Solves what happens when yesterday's fact is superseded. Reference: Graphiti (Apache-2.0). Benchmark: temporal QA, contradiction handling, delayed events, superseded facts, historical queries, stale-answer frequency. Shared rules for the retrieval and memory program: a source document, repo

results.title: Native graph storage and a cost-based graph/vector query planner
results.author: zeekay
results.body_snippet: Choose vector-first, graph-first, pure traversal or a cached neighbourhood from estimated candidate counts, selectivity, graph degree and latency budget. Start with an embedded graph representation and compact adjacency indexes; use Apache AGE (graph in PostgreSQL), NebulaGraph and Cognee as scalability and design baselines; no separate distributed graph cluster until measurements justify one. results.author: paolino
results.body_snippet: **In plain words.** On chain, a conviction pays the deposit only to the payee of a bounty commitment opened beforehand over this checkpoint and this evidence. That is what stops the producer of a block from copying a conviction and paying itself (#271). The Lean does not say this: its conviction step (`Checkpoint.Step.convict`) accepts any payee as soon as duplicity holds. The code is therefore stricter than the model. results.title: parse_duration drops the days (d) unit
results.author: tine1117
results.body_snippet: ## Bug `parse_duration` silently drops the **days** (`d`) unit. The README lists `d` as a supported unit, but the parser ignores it and returns a wrong (too-small) result instead of raising or counting it. ### Reproduction ```python from duration_utils import parse_duration parse_duration("1d") # -> 0 (expected 86400) parse_duration("2d4h") # -> 14400 (expected 187200) ``` ### Expected `d` should be counted as 86400 seconds, so `parse_duration("1d") == 86400` and `parse_duration("2d4h") == 18720
